bills.title: Protecting Privacy in Purchases Act
bills.status: Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
bills.nexus: H.R. 1181 would restrict the collection and sale of consumer purchase data, implicating Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and the Office of Terrorism and Financial Intelligence because such data feeds anti-money laundering and suspicious activity monitoring programs. If enacted, compliance obligations on financial institutions could narrow the transaction data available for Bank Secrecy Act reporting, creating a tension between privacy mandates and Treasury's illicit finance detection authorities.

bills.title: To direct the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to establish a pilot program to use four-dimensional functional lung imaging software product to identify respiratory disorders and lung disease in veterans, and for other purposes.
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
bills.nexus: This bill has no direct nexus to Treasury, as it directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs — not Treasury or any Treasury bureau — to establish a medical imaging pilot program. Unless a revenue, tax, sanctions, or financial regulation component emerges during markup, Treasury has no implementation role or material risk exposure here.

bills.title: Failing Bank Acquisition Fairness Act
bills.status: Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
bills.nexus: H.R. 6556 would amend the rules governing emergency acquisitions of failing banks, directly implicating Treasury's authorities under the Federal Deposit Insurance Act and its coordination role with the FDIC and OCC during systemic-risk determinations. The implementation risk centers on potential constraints to Treasury's ability to facilitate rapid failing-bank transactions, which could slow crisis response and increase resolution costs to the Deposit Insurance Fund.

bills.title: Budgeting for a Better America Act
bills.status: Referred to the Committee on the Budget, and in addition to the Committee on Rules, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9452 would restructure the federal budget process, directly implicating Treasury's Office of Fiscal Assistant Secretary and its debt management and cash flow forecasting functions. If enacted, changes to spending caps, budget enforcement mechanisms, or baseline rules could constrain Treasury's borrowing authorities and complicate debt limit and appropriations timing projections.

bills.title: Keep Public Funds in Public Schools Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9289 falls within Treasury's jurisdiction because it would modify or restrict tax-code provisions, likely Section 529 or related education savings and tax-credit mechanisms, that the IRS administers under Treasury's authority. The implementation risk centers on Treasury and IRS needing to issue guidance, update plan agreements, and potentially retool compliance frameworks if existing education tax benefits are curtailed or redirected away from private school expenses.

bills.title: Bipartisan Transparency for American Taxpayers Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
bills.nexus: Without a known nexus or bill text provided, I cannot reliably identify which specific Treasury office or authority H.R. 8955 touches, and fabricating that link would risk misinforming a legislative affairs team. bills.title: No WAR Act
bills.status: Referred to the Committee on Rules, and in addition to the Committee on the Budget, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
bills.nexus: H.R. 8592 touches budget process rules that govern how spending and revenue legislation moves through Congress, implicating Treasury's role in executing fiscal policy and managing borrowing authority under the debt limit. If enacted, changes to waiver or reconciliation procedures could constrain or accelerate revenue and appropriations measures that Treasury must implement, creating planning and cash-management risk.

bills.title: To amend the Congressional Budget and Impoundment Control Act of 1974 to establish certain procedures for consideration of annual appropriation bills, and for other purposes.
bills.status: Referred to the Committee on Rules, and in addition to the Committee on the Budget, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
bills.nexus: H.R. 8380 amends the Impoundment Control Act of 1974, which directly governs Treasury's authority to withhold or delay appropriated funds and shapes the annual discretionary spending framework Treasury executes through apportionment and cash management. Changes to appropriations procedures affect Treasury's Office of Management and Budget coordination role, debt ceiling headroom calculations, and the timing of borrowing operations managed by the Bureau of the Fiscal Service.

bills.title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to establish tax credits for the production of, and investment in, certain renewable materials.
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 8137 directly implicates IRS and Treasury's Office of Tax Policy because it would add new production and investment tax credit provisions to the Internal Revenue Code, requiring Treasury to issue implementing regulations and eligibility guidance. The principal risks include revenue cost uncertainty, definitional ambiguity around "renewable materials" that could broaden credit claims beyond legislative intent, and administrative burden on IRS to verify qualifying production and investment activity.

bills.title: Tribal Tax and Investment Reform Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means, and in addition to the Committee on Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
bills.nexus: H.R. 7705 directly implicates the Office of Tax Policy and IRS, as it would modify federal tax treatment of tribal governments and likely alter tribal economic development bond authorities under the Internal Revenue Code. Treasury faces implementation risk in administering any new tribal tax parity provisions and potential revenue scoring exposure if investment incentives expand tribal entities' tax-exempt financing capacity.

bills.title: No Tax on Takings Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 7687 would exclude compensation received for government takings of property from gross income, directly implicating IRS authority under the Internal Revenue Code and the Joint Committee on Taxation's revenue scoring process. Treasury's Office of Tax Policy would need to assess the revenue cost and potential for taxpayers to recharacterize other transactions as takings to exploit the exclusion.

bills.title: United States Foreign Service Commemorative Coin Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.
bills.nexus: H.R. 6126 directs the Secretary of the Treasury to mint and issue commemorative coins honoring the U.S. Foreign Service, directly engaging the U.S. Mint under Treasury's authority pursuant to 31 U.S.C. Chapter 51. Treasury's implementation risk centers on production cost recovery, surcharge fund management, and ensuring the coin program does not exceed statutory mintage limits or create unbudgeted obligations for the Mint.

bills.title: To amend the Bank Secrecy Act to exempt transactions with respect to cash reward payments by crime stopper organizations from certain currency transaction reports.
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.
bills.nexus: H.R. 6029 directly implicates FinCEN's authority under the Bank Secrecy Act, which Treasury administers, because it would carve out a new statutory exemption from the Currency Transaction Report filing requirement for cash payments made by crime stopper organizations. Treasury's implementation risk centers on FinCEN needing to define qualifying organizations, update its CTR exemption regulations, and assess whether the carve-out could create an exploitable gap in the anti-money-laundering reporting framework.

bills.title: Azerbaijan Sanctions Review Act of 2025
bills.status: Referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
bills.nexus: H.R. 5369 would require a review of sanctions related to Azerbaijan, directly implicating OFAC's authority to administer and enforce sanctions programs under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act. Treasury's implementation risk centers on potential statutory constraints on OFAC's discretionary designation and delisting decisions, which could complicate existing sanctions architecture and interagency coordination with State.

bills.title: Tackling Predatory Litigation Funding Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 3512 falls within Treasury's purview because litigation finance arrangements can implicate tax treatment of returns paid to funders, a matter under IRS jurisdiction within Treasury. The bill's disclosure and restriction provisions could require Treasury and IRS to issue guidance or regulations governing how funding proceeds and repayments are characterized and reported for federal tax purposes.

bills.title: Tax Relief for Victims of Crimes, Scams, and Disasters Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 3469 directly implicates the Internal Revenue Service and the Office of Tax Policy because it would amend the Internal Revenue Code to expand exclusions or deductions for losses suffered by crime, fraud, and disaster victims. Treasury's implementation concern centers on IRS's capacity to administer new eligibility criteria, verify qualifying losses at scale, and estimate the resulting revenue cost accurately for scoring purposes.

bills.title: Renewable Natural Gas Incentive Act of 2025
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 2596 falls squarely within Treasury's purview because it would amend the Internal Revenue Code to create or expand tax incentives for renewable natural gas, implicating the Office of Tax Policy and likely IRS guidance obligations. Treasury's implementation risk centers on defining qualifying fuel pathways, administering any credit or deduction mechanism, and preventing improper claims that could erode revenue.

bills.title: Supporting Innovation in Agriculture Act of 2025
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 1705 was referred to Ways and Means, signaling it likely involves tax code changes such as credits, deductions, or expensing rules related to agricultural innovation, which fall within IRS and Office of Tax Policy jurisdiction. Treasury's implementation risk centers on designing or administering any new tax incentives without creating compliance gaps, revenue scoring uncertainty, or unintended interaction with existing Sec. 179 or R&D credit provisions.

bills.title: Veterans Member Business Loan Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.
bills.nexus: H.R. 507 would expand credit union member business lending limits for veteran-owned businesses, directly implicating Treasury's Office of Financial Institutions and its role in overseeing federal credit policy frameworks. Treasury monitors this because loosened lending caps could shift credit risk exposure across the federally insured credit union system, requiring assessment of potential impacts on the National Credit Union Share Insurance Fund and broader financial stability.

bills.title: READY Accounts Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 440 would create tax-advantaged savings accounts, directly implicating IRS and Treasury's Office of Tax Policy, which would need to design qualifying rules, contribution limits, and reporting requirements. The implementation risk centers on IRS systems capacity to administer a new account type and Treasury's need to issue guidance reconciling READY accounts with existing tax-preferred savings vehicles.
